title: Rational points detect stable subspaces for smooth affine groups
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $G$ be a smooth affine group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. A rational representation is a homomorphism $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$, with the general linear group interpreted after a basis choice as [def-sc-general-linear-group]; for $V=0$ it is the trivial group scheme. For every $k$-linear subspace $W\subseteq V$, the following conditions are equivalent: (i) $\rho_k(g)W=W$ for every $g\in G(k)$; (ii) for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and every $g\in G(A)$ one has $\rho_A(g)(W\otimes_k A)=W\otimes_k A$. In condition (ii) the tensors are viewed as submodules of $V\otimes_k A$.

source.place: Corollaries 4.4--4.5, printed p.85, with Proposition 4.3 (closed subspace stabilizer); Propositions 1.10--1.12 for schematic density of rational points of a reduced scheme over an algebraically closed field.

proof.text: Condition (ii) implies (i) by taking $A=k$ and the canonical identification $W\otimes_k k=W$. If $V=0$, then $W=0$ and both conditions hold. Hence assume $n=\dim_k V>0$ and (i).

source.place: Proposition 4.3 and Corollaries 4.4--4.5, printed p.85; Proposition 1.10, printed pp.9--10

proof.text: Choose a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $V$ whose first $r$ vectors form a basis of $W$. For every $k$-algebra $A$, these give $V\otimes_k A=A^n$ and identify $W\otimes_k A$ with the first $r$ coordinates: the projection onto their span is a left inverse to the inclusion, also after tensoring. Let $B=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$. Pulling back the matrix coordinate $x_{ij}$ along $\rho$ gives $b_{ij}\in B$. By the coordinate description of $\mathrm{GL}_{n,k}$, for $g:\operatorname{Spec}A\to G$ the matrix of $\rho_A(g)$ has entries $g^*(b_{ij})$. Thus its image of $W\otimes_k A$ is contained in $W\otimes_k A$ exactly when $g^*(b_{ij})=0$ for $i>r$, $j\le r$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3 and Corollaries 4.4--4.5, printed p.85; Proposition 1.10, printed pp.9--10

proof.text: Apply [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] to $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its fibre over the unique point is $G$, so $G$ is reduced. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] choose an affine open cover $U_a=\operatorname{Spec}B_a$ of $G$ with each $B_a$ finitely generated over $k$. By [def-pc-reduced-scheme], each section ring $B_a$ is reduced. These are precisely the hypotheses needed for the vanishing principle on each chart.

source.place: Tag 056T, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal; finite-type affine cover and reduced section rings as in the cited definitions

proof.text: Fix $i>r$, $j\le r$. Every $k$-point $u$ of $U_a$ gives a $k$-point $g$ of $G$. Hypothesis (i) and the coordinate calculation in step 2 give $b_{ij}(g)=0$. Hence $b_{ij}|_{U_a}$ vanishes at every $k$-point of $\operatorname{Spec}B_a$. Clause (2) of [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing] applies because $k$ is algebraically closed and $B_a$ is reduced and finitely generated; it gives $b_{ij}|_{U_a}=0$. Sections equal on an open cover are equal, so $b_{ij}=0$ in $B$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3 and Corollaries 4.4--4.5, printed p.85; Proposition 1.10, printed pp.9--10

proof.text: For any $k$-algebra $A$ and $g\in G(A)$, evaluation sends these zero $b_{ij}$ to zero. Step 2 therefore gives $\rho_A(g)(W\otimes_k A)\subseteq W\otimes_k A$. The same assertion for $g^{-1}\in G(A)$ gives the reverse inclusion after applying $\rho_A(g)$, since $\rho_A(g)\rho_A(g^{-1})=1$. This proves (ii), including $r=0$ and $r=n$, when the relevant coordinate equations are empty. The zero algebra also causes no exception: both tensor modules are zero.

source.place: Proposition 4.3 and Corollaries 4.4--4.5, printed p.85; Proposition 1.10, printed pp.9--10
